tool.name: OpenRefine
tool.command:
#import re export IMPORT_DIR="\$(pwd)/imports" && mkdir -p imports exports &&
## Stage datasets in the job directory. The running number keeps ## the names unique, the cleaned element identifier keeps them ## meaningful: each file becomes an OpenRefine project of that name. ## With multiple="true" and no dataset selected Galaxy still yields a ## list with one None-like entry, so each item must be truth-checked. #for $count, $file in enumerate($input): #if $file #set $cleaned_name = str($count + 1) + '_' + re.sub('[^\\w\\-\\.\\s]', '_', str($file.element_identifier)) cp '$file' 'imports/${cleaned_name}.${file.file_ext}' && #end if #end for
#if $run_mode.mode == 'headless' #if not $input echo 'ERROR: headless mode requires at least one input dataset' >&2 && exit 1 && #end if #if $run_mode.recipe cp '$run_mode.recipe' 'imports/.galaxy-recipe.json' && #end if python3 /galaxy_io.py headless --exports-dir "\$(pwd)/exports" --format '$run_mode.export_format' #else export PROXY_PREFIX="\${EP_PATH%/}" && bash /startup.sh #end if

param.name: input
param.label: Datasets to import as OpenRefine projects
param.help: Each dataset becomes a separate OpenRefine project named after the dataset. In interactive mode more data can be imported at any later time using the dedicated 'Galaxy - OpenRefine' page.

param.name: mode
param.label: Run mode
param.help: Interactive opens OpenRefine in your browser. Headless runs without a user interface: data is loaded, the optional recipe is applied and the results are exported.
param.option: Run as normal tool: load data, apply recipe, export

param.name: recipe
param.label: OpenRefine operations JSON (recipe)
param.help: The recorded workflow, as exported by OpenRefine's 'Extract operations' dialog or by the 'Operations (.json)' button on the app's Galaxy - OpenRefine page. It is applied to every imported dataset; the columns it references must exist in them.

tool.help:
`OpenRefine <https://openrefine.org/>`_ (previously Google Refine) is a powerful tool for working with messy data: cleaning it; transforming it from one format into another; and extending it with web services and external data.
**Interactive mode** (default)
A private OpenRefine session is started and opened in your browser.
- *Import:* datasets selected in the tool form are imported as OpenRefine projects when the session starts; the project name is the dataset name. Further datasets from the current Galaxy history can be imported at any time from the *Galaxy - OpenRefine* page of the app: a link at the bottom of the OpenRefine window opens it (it is the entry point URL with ``io/`` appended). OpenRefine's own *Import project* menu restores previously exported ``.openrefine.tar.gz`` project archives. - *Export:* the *Galaxy - OpenRefine* page exports into your Galaxy history: project **rows** as ``TSV``, ``CSV`` or ``XLSX`` (all current edits are included; facets and filters are not applied - use OpenRefine's own *Export* menu for filtered or custom exports), the native **project archive** (``.openrefine.tar.gz``) as a resumable session, and the recorded **operations JSON** (the re-appliable workflow, see the headless mode below). Uploaded datasets appear directly in your Galaxy history, also while the session is still running. The *OpenRefine results* collection shown in the history stays empty in interactive mode. - *Close the app:* use the *Export everything and close* button on the *Galaxy - OpenRefine* page: it exports every project (rows as TSV plus the project archive) to your Galaxy history and then stops the session. If any export fails, the session stays open and can be retried. Wait for running OpenRefine operations to finish before closing; closing the browser tab or an idle-timeout shutdown does **not** perform a final export.
**Tool mode** (no browser needed)
Runs the whole workflow without a user interface: the selected datasets are loaded as OpenRefine projects, the optional **operations JSON** recipe is applied to every project, and the results are exported and returned as the *OpenRefine results* collection - one dataset per input, in the chosen format. The job finishes on its own; nothing is left running. This makes the step usable inside workflows.
To get a recipe, clean a dataset once in an interactive OpenRefine session and export its recorded operations (*Extract operations* dialog in OpenRefine, or the *Operations (.json)* button on the *Galaxy - OpenRefine* page). The recipe is a list of OpenRefine operations in JSON form and is applied to **every** imported dataset, so all of them must contain the columns it references. A recipe is optional: without one, the mode simply loads and re-exports the data (e.g. to convert XLSX to TSV).
For XLSX and ODS inputs, all sheets are imported into one project. The first row of each sheet is used as its column header.
